title.value: Offline Retrieval Evaluation Without Evaluation Metrics
title.justification: The title of the paper clearly states the focus on evaluating retrieval systems without traditional evaluation metrics.
title.quote: Offline Retrieval Evaluation Without Evaluation Metrics

extractions.description: The paper introduces a metric-free evaluation method for offline information retrieval and recommendation systems, called recall-paired preference (RPP). This method simulates user subpopulations and compares system rankings based on preferences across these pseudo-populations, without collapsing differences into a single metric. RPP is shown to improve discriminative power and maintain robustness compared to traditional metrics.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central focus of the paper is on improving information retrieval systems' evaluation methods. While these systems may have applications in various sectors including climate-related fields, the primary objective of the paper is not tied to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Offline evaluation of information retrieval and recommendation has traditionally focused on distilling the quality of a ranking into a scalar metric... Although evaluation metrics provide a... summary of system performance, they also collapse subtle differences across users into a single number... We propose recall-paired preference (RPP), a metric-free evaluation method based on directly computing a preference between ranked lists.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on technical aspects of information retrieval evaluation and does not directly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: Our results across multiple search and recommendation tasks demonstrate that RPP substantially improves discriminative power while correlating well with existing metrics and being equally robust to incomplete data.

primary_sub_category.justification: Since the primary focus is not related to climate or ecological sustainability, a specific sub-category does not apply here.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose rank-paired preference (RPP), an evaluation method that addresses concerns both about label efficiency and robustness to user behavior.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new sustainable development category as it is not related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: We present results reflecting that RPP can capture existing metrics' properties while offering better sensitivity.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on evaluation methods in information retrieval, which does not align with traditional Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We propose recall-paired preference (RPP), which is an evaluation method for offline information retrieval systems.
